newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: CRICKET-ENGLAND TOIL AGAINST ZIMBABWE SEAMERS.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ENGLAND TOIL AGAINST ZIMBABWE SEAMERS.

text.p: Zimbabwe made the most of helpful seam bowling conditions to leave England reeling on 108 for six at tea on the opening day of the second test on Thursday.
Heath Streak undermined the innings with three for 24 and medium pacer Guy Whittall took two for nine after England were put in to bat.

On a steamy morning with the ball swinging about, Nick Knight was the first to go when he shaped to leg glance paceman Henry Olonga's first ball, got a thin edge and was caught by wicketkeeper Andy Flower for 13.
Captain Mike Atherton had made 15 he drove loosely at a wide ball from Whittall and edged to Alistair Campbell at first slip.

In the previous over from Streak, Campbell had dropped a simple chance from Alec Stewart, but it did not cost Zimbabwe anything. In Streak's next over Stewart drilled a cover drive straight to Grant Flower to be caught for 19.
England, 63 for three at lunch, were immediately in more trouble after the interval, losing the out-of-form Graham Thorpe for five, caught by Mark Dekker at short leg off Streak.

Nasser Hussain and John Crawley dropped anchor, but in an attempt to break the shackles Hussain drove at a wide one from Streak and was brilliantly caught behind by the diving Andy Flower, who took the catch to the right of first slip. Hussain made 11.
All-rounder Craig White arrived for his first innings since joining the touring side as cover for the injured Ronnie Irani with the scoreboard showing 73 for five.
He was lucky to survive an lbw appeal from leg-spinner Paul Strang when he had made seven, but did not last much longer.
Whittall picked up his second wicket when White, on nine, steered a ball straight to Campbell at first slip, leaving John Crawley unbeaten on 23 at tea and Robert Croft two not out.
